cards.text: David wrote this song for the choirmaster, back when he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah. The heading says Joab, commander of David's army (2 Samuel 8:16), came back and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Now David starts talking straight to God, and I'm leaning in like it's the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: David opens his song talking straight to God. What does David say God has done to His people?

cards.text: Rejected, broken, angry. David does NOT tiptoe around God, he walks right in and puts it ALL on the counter, then finishes with one big ask: 'restore us!'

cards.question: David keeps going with a picture. What does he say God has done to the land?

answers.text: Shaken it and torn it open
Dried it out with no rain

cards.question: David asks God to heal the land's fractures, because the land is ___.
Next, David tells God that His people have had nothing but easy days. True or false?

cards.text: David says God has shown His people hardship, and they're staggered from the wine He made them drink. I know staggering, friend: my first hop on this gold base after years lying flat in a drawer, I wobbled around the bakery like a newborn deer on ICE.
Then the song turns. For those who fear Him, God has raised a banner, and friend, after all that shaking and staggering, that banner is the first thing in this whole song that goes UP.

cards.question: God has raised a banner for those who fear Him. What's it there for?

answers.text: So they can flee the bow
So they can mark the border
So they can count the troops

cards.text: Then comes 'Selah,' and GOOD, because I needed a breather after all that. When the song picks back up, David asks God to respond with His right hand.

cards.question: David asks God to respond with His right hand. What does he want God to do?

cards.text: Now David brings in God's own words. God has spoken from His sanctuary, and friend, when GOD speaks, the whole bakery goes quiet. Even the ovens.

cards.question: David has been praying about rejection and hardship. Then come God's words from His sanctuary. How do they open?

cards.text: God says, 'I will triumph!' Then He reads out the land like a boss going down the shift schedule, Shechem, the Valley of Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh, and NOBODY gets the day off.

cards.question: God says He'll parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth. What's He showing about this land?

answers.text: It's too far gone to save

cards.question: God calls Ephraim His helmet and Judah His scepter. What do those two pictures have in common?

answers.text: Things God is still looking for

cards.text: Then God turns to the nations nearby. Moab is His washbasin, and upon Edom He tosses His sandal, and friend, out of everybody on that list, I would NOT want to be the one catching the SANDAL.

cards.question: Over Philistia, God says He'll weep in sorrow. True or false?

cards.text: Over Philistia, God shouts in triumph. That's the end of God's words, and now David's back with a question of his own.

cards.question: David asks, 'Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to ___?'

cards.text: Then David asks, 'Have You not rejected us, O God?' There's that word again, rejected, back like an oven timer I SWEAR I already turned off.

cards.question: In that same breath, David asks if God will no longer do something with their armies. What is it?

cards.text: Next, David asks God for aid against the enemy. And he doesn't leave anybody guessing why it has to come from God, he says it right out loud.

cards.question: Why does David say the aid against the enemy has to come from God?

answers.text: The help of man is worthless

cards.text: Worthless, he says, and I believe it: the dead batteries I shared that drawer with SWORE they still had a little charge left. Love 'em, friend, but not one of them ever lit a THING.

cards.question: In the last line of the song, David says God will trample their enemies. True or false?

cards.text: And there it is: 'With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.' The fight's still out there, but David knows who he's going in with, and friend, that changes EVERYTHING.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 4 of the 6 choice cards are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 9 and 11). There is only 1 fill in the blank and 1 true or false.

findings.problem: Card 1 only gives the heading, which reports a victory (Joab striking down 12,000 Edomites). Nothing hints that the song opens as a lament. A thoughtful baker reasoning from card 1 would lean toward 'Lifted them high,' so the setup points away from the right answer 'Rejected them.' Card 1 needs to signal the shift, for example that David's words to God are not what you'd expect after a win.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke makes God the punchline. It casts God declaring His ownership of the land as a boss going down a shift schedule where 'NOBODY gets the day off,' which pictures God as a demanding boss.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't hold together. Verses 6 and 7 are about parceling out land and claiming it ('Gilead is Mine'). Places like Shechem and Gilead can't get a day off, so 'NOBODY gets the day off' has no clear match to the text, and a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: 4. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. 5. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
